```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 8
    n_vehicles = 3
    Q = 57  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[20, 13], [29, 10], [87, 56], [29, 8], [13, 8], [44, 62], [18, 90], [34, 75]]
    demands = [25, 8, 19, 13, 10, 7, 8, 24]
    time_windows = [[0, 338], [44, 130], [55, 149], [36, 124], [70, 168], [59, 149], [30, 89], [47, 124], [39, 115]]
    service_times = [10, 5, 13, 6, 15, 10, 11, 6]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Routing and Scheduling Challenge for Today’s Delivery Wave

Overview
We are planning a delivery wave from our central depot using a fleet of identical vehicles. All deployed vehicles will depart the depot at time 0, complete a single continuous tour to serve assigned customers, and return to the depot before the facility closes for the day. Travel time between any two locations is based on straight-line distance, with an implicit speed of 1 (distance units equal time units).

Delivery Challenge
- Every customer must be visited exactly once during this wave.
- Each customer has a defined delivery time window; the start of unloading must fall within this window. If a vehicle arrives early, it will wait until the window opens.
- Each stop requires a non-zero service (unloading) time; the vehicle departs a customer after the arrival time plus service time, or after the window opens plus service time if it arrived early.
- Each vehicle performs a single trip: depart at time 0, visit a sequence of customers, and return to the depot before closing.

Capacity and Loading Requirements
- Each customer has a pickup/delivery demand. The sum of demands assigned to any one vehicle must not exceed that vehicle’s carrying capacity at any point on its route.
- Customer orders are not splittable across vehicles; one vehicle is responsible for the full demand of each assigned customer.

Cost Structure
- Activating a vehicle incurs a fixed deployment cost, regardless of distance traveled.
- In-route costs scale with total travel distance. The planning task must balance the trade-off between activating more vehicles (to relieve time windows and reduce travel on individual tours) and consolidating stops on fewer vehicles (to save fixed deployment costs), while still returning all vehicles before depot closing.

Planning Goal
Our objective is to design routes and departure/arrival schedules that:
- Serve every customer exactly once within their time window.
- Respect vehicle capacity limits and service times at each stop.
- Ensure all vehicles depart at time 0 and return to the depot before it closes.
- Minimize the sum of total travel distance and vehicle deployment costs.

Key Assumptions
- Vehicles are identical in capacity and performance.
- Travel time equals straight-line distance between mapped coordinates, with an implicit speed of 1.
- Waiting is permitted for early arrivals; late arrivals are not permitted.
- Each vehicle operates a single tour in this planning horizon.
